Repo root: /opt/nxeon-wt-paymentui (a git worktree of the Nxeon Next.js/TS/Prisma/Postgres platform, Stripe payments). I need a detailed map of the existing checkout/payment architecture before building a new embedded payment UI. Please answer ALL of the following, quoting exact file paths, function names, and key line ranges/snippets (not full file dumps):

1. lib/stripe.ts — list every exported `create*CheckoutSession`-style function (createOrderCheckout, createGameOrderCheckout, createHostOrderCheckout, createResizeCheckout, createDiskExpandCheckout, any others). For each: what params it takes, what Stripe API it calls (checkout.sessions.create? paymentIntents.create?), what metadata it attaches, whether/how it sets `customer` and `setup_future_usage` for saved-card behavior, and what success/cancel URLs it uses.

2. lib/fulfil-checkout.ts — the full shape of the fulfillment entry point(s). What function(s) get called after a successful payment (e.g. fulfilCheckout / fulfillOrder etc), what input they expect (session object? metadata bag? specific fields), what side effects happen (DB writes, provisioning trigger, emails), and whether there's already any abstraction that isn't Stripe-specific (i.e. does it take a Stripe object directly or a normalized metadata object?).

3. The webhook handler(s) that call into lib/fulfil-checkout.ts — find app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts or equivalent. What events does it listen for (checkout.session.completed, payment_intent.succeeded, etc), how does it verify the Stripe signature, and exactly how does it invoke fulfillment.

4. test/checkout-metadata.test.ts — summarize what it asserts (which functions it tests, and the exact expectations around customer + setup_future_usage attachment). Quote the key assertions.

5. The wizard components for VPS, Shared Hosting, Game Servers, and Business Email deploy flows, and the resize/disk-expand upgrade flow — find their Review step components (search for "Review" step, "createOrderCheckout", "createGameOrderCheckout", "createHostOrderCheckout", "createResizeCheckout", "createDiskExpandCheckout" usages in app/ or components/). List the file paths of each Review step component and how each currently redirects to Stripe (e.g. `stripe.redirectToCheckout` or `window.location = session.url`).

6. components/customer/WizardTrustBar.tsx and components/customer/PaymentTrustBar.tsx — full content of both files. Also note the HONESTY comment mentioned about money-back guarantee claims.

7. Optional-integration gating pattern: find `gscConfigured()` (Google Search Console gate) — show its implementation and one example of how a feature checks it and hides/disables UI when env vars are absent. This is the pattern new PayPal/Coinbase gating should follow.

8. Support channels: check lib/kb-system.ts, any live chat widget component, and any "support ticket" system. What real support channels exist today (live chat widget file path, support email address used elsewhere in the codebase, any ticket system)?

9. package.json — current Stripe-related and payment-related dependencies (stripe, @stripe/stripe-js, @stripe/react-stripe-js, any paypal or coinbase packages already present).

10. Test running setup: how are tests run (npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts)? Roughly how many test files are there in test/, and are there any existing webhook-signature-verification tests to use as a pattern (e.g. for Stripe webhook signature checks)?

Be thorough but concise — use file:line references and short quoted snippets rather than full file contents where files are long. This is pure research, no code changes.

596	/**
597	 * Classify a retrieved session. Pure — no clock, no network, no database — so the
598	 * routing decision is unit-testable and identical for the redirect and the webhook.
599	 */
600	export function classifyCheckoutSession(
601	  session: Pick<Stripe.Checkout.Session, "metadata" | "payment_status">,
602	): CheckoutPurpose {
603	  const md = session.metadata ?? null;
604	  const userId = parseId(md?.nxeonUserId);
605	  if (!userId || session.payment_status !== "paid") return { kind: "unpaid" };
606	
607	  const orderRaw = md?.nxeonOrder;
608	  if (orderRaw) {
609	    let intent: unknown;
610	    try {
611	      intent = JSON.parse(orderRaw);
612	    } catch {
613	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonOrder is not valid JSON" };
614	    }
615	    if (!intent || typeof intent !== "object") {
616	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonOrder is not an object" };
617	    }
618	    return {
619	      kind: "order",
620	      userId,
621	      intent: intent as OrderIntent,
622	      sold: parseOrderPrice(session.metadata?.nxeonOrderPrice),
623	      campaign: sanitizeCampaign(md?.nxeonPromoCampaign),
624	      promoReservationToken: parseId(md?.nxeonPromoReservation),
625	      couponReservationToken: parseId(md?.nxeonCouponReservation),
626	    };
627	  }
628	
629	  const gameRaw = md?.nxeonGameOrder;
630	  if (gameRaw) {
631	    let slim: Record<string, unknown>;
632	    try {
633	      slim = JSON.parse(gameRaw) as Record<string, unknown>;
634	    } catch {
635	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonGameOrder is not valid JSON" };
636	    }
637	    if (!slim || typeof slim !== "object") {
638	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonGameOrder is not an object" };
639	    }
640	    const gamePlanId = parseId(slim.gamePlanId);
641	    if (!gamePlanId) {
642	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonGameOrder is missing gamePlanId" };
643	    }
644	    // The gameplay config rides in its own optional key; a missing/garbled blob is
645	    // simply dropped (placeGameOrder fills defaults), never treated as unreadable —
646	    // it is not money and cannot change the settled charge.
647	    let config: Record<string, unknown> | null = null;
648	    const rawCfg = md?.nxeonGameConfig;
649	    if (typeof rawCfg === "string" && rawCfg !== "") {
650	      try {
651	        const p = JSON.parse(rawCfg);
652	        if (p && typeof p === "object") config = p as Record<string, unknown>;
653	      } catch {
654	        config = null;
655	      }
656	    }
657	    const intent: GameOrderIntent = {
658	      gamePlanId,
659	      termMonths: typeof slim.termMonths === "number" ? slim.termMonths : 1,
660	      serverName: typeof slim.serverName === "string" ? slim.serverName : undefined,
661	      hostname: typeof slim.hostname === "string" ? slim.hostname : undefined,
662	      variant: typeof slim.variant === "string" ? slim.variant : undefined,
663	      config,
664	    };
665	    return { kind: "gameOrder", userId, intent, sold: parseGameOrderPrice(md?.nxeonGameOrderPrice) };
666	  }
667	
668	  const resizeRaw = md?.nxeonResize;
669	  if (resizeRaw) {
670	    let p: Record<string, unknown>;
671	    try {
672	      p = JSON.parse(resizeRaw) as Record<string, unknown>;
673	    } catch {
674	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonResize is not valid JSON" };
675	    }
676	    const serverId = parseId(p?.serverId);
677	    const planId = parseId(p?.planId);
678	    const chargeCents = parseChargeCents(p?.chargeCents);
679	    if (!serverId || !planId || chargeCents === null) {
680	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonResize is missing serverId/planId/chargeCents" };
681	    }
682	    return { kind: "resize", userId, serverId, planId, chargeCents };
683	  }
684	
685	  const expandRaw = md?.nxeonDiskExpand;
686	  if (expandRaw) {
687	    let p: Record<string, unknown>;
688	    try {
689	      p = JSON.parse(expandRaw) as Record<string, unknown>;
690	    } catch {
691	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonDiskExpand is not valid JSON" };
692	    }
693	    const serverId = parseId(p?.serverId);
694	    const addGB = parseChargeCents(p?.addGB);
695	    const chargeCents = parseChargeCents(p?.chargeCents);
696	    if (!serverId || addGB === null || chargeCents === null) {
697	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonDiskExpand is missing serverId/addGB/chargeCents" };
698	    }
699	    return { kind: "diskExpand", userId, serverId, addGB, chargeCents };
700	  }
701	
702	  // Shared-hosting order funded by card. The full order inputs ride in nxeonHostOrder;
703	  // `planId` and `idempotencyKey` are the two fields fulfilment cannot proceed without
704	  // (the key governs the `hostorder:<key>` placement claim), so a payload missing
705	  // either is `unreadable`, never a silent top-up.
706	  const hostRaw = md?.nxeonHostOrder;
707	  if (hostRaw) {
708	    let p: Record<string, unknown>;
709	    try {
710	      p = JSON.parse(hostRaw) as Record<string, unknown>;
711	    } catch {
712	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonHostOrder is not valid JSON" };
713	    }
714	    const planId = parseId(p?.planId);
715	    const idempotencyKey = parseId(p?.idempotencyKey);
716	    if (!planId || !idempotencyKey) {
717	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonHostOrder is missing planId/idempotencyKey" };
718	    }
719	    const intent: HostOrderCheckoutIntent = {
720	      planId,
721	      idempotencyKey,
722	      domain: typeof p.domain === "string" ? p.domain : undefined,
723	      subdomainLabel: typeof p.subdomainLabel === "string" ? p.subdomainLabel : undefined,
724	      extraDiskGB: typeof p.extraDiskGB === "number" ? p.extraDiskGB : undefined,
725	      termMonths: typeof p.termMonths === "number" ? p.termMonths : undefined,
726	      appSlug: typeof p.appSlug === "string" ? p.appSlug : undefined,
727	    };
728	    return { kind: "hostOrder", userId, intent };
729	  }
730	
731	  // Business-email order funded by card. domainName + emailPlanId are load-bearing.
732	  const emailRaw = md?.nxeonEmailOrder;
733	  if (emailRaw) {
734	    let p: Record<string, unknown>;
735	    try {
736	      p = JSON.parse(emailRaw) as Record<string, unknown>;
737	    } catch {
738	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonEmailOrder is not valid JSON" };
739	    }
740	    const domainName = parseId(p?.domainName);
741	    const emailPlanId = parseId(p?.emailPlanId);
742	    if (!domainName || !emailPlanId) {
743	      return { kind: "unreadable", userId, detail: "nxeonEmailOrder is missing domainName/emailPlanId" };
744	    }
745	    const intent: EmailOrderCheckoutIntent = {
746	      domainName,
747	      emailPlanId,
748	      termMonths: typeof p.termMonths === "number" ? p.termMonths : undefined,
749	    };
750	    return { kind: "emailOrder", userId, intent };
751	  }
752	
753	  return { kind: "topup", userId };
754	}
755	
756	/**
757	 * Retrieve a Checkout session ONCE. Throws when Stripe cannot be read — the caller
758	 * must never be able to mistake a transport failure for "this session is a top-up".
759	 */
760	export async function retrieveCheckoutSession(sessionId: string): Promise<Stripe.Checkout.Session> {
761	  if (!stripeConfigured()) throw new Error("Stripe is not configured");
762	  return stripe().checkout.sessions.retrieve(sessionId);
763	}
764	
765	/** Retrieve + classify in one step. Throws on a Stripe read failure, never lies. */
766	export async function getCheckoutPurpose(sessionId: string): Promise<CheckoutPurpose> {
767	  return classifyCheckoutSession(await retrieveCheckoutSession(sessionId));
768	}
769	
770	/**
771	 * True when this session's card payment is the FUNDING LEG of a purchase — a VPS
772	 * order, an upgrade, a disk expansion — rather than a wallet top-up the customer
773	 * bought for its own sake.
774	 *
775	 * The wallet is the settlement bus for every card-paid purchase: the card amount
776	 * is credited in, then the purchase debits the full total back out. That credit is
777	 * plumbing, not a product, and it must not be documented as one.
778	 *
779	 * REAL INCIDENT (2026-07-26 rehearsal, H3): every paid session got a PAID "Wallet
780	 * top-up" invoice here AND a PAID invoice from whatever it funded, so one $82.53
781	 * annual purchase produced `Wallet top-up $82.53` + `Starter VPS — Annual $82.53`
782	 * and the invoices page reported $165.06 paid lifetime — a customer reconciling
783	 * against their card statement saw twice their spend. Each document was internally
784	 * consistent; there were simply two of them for one payment. worker/billing.ts
785	 * already states the rule for the renewal path: "No invoice for the card leg …
786	 * a second document for the card portion would double-count the same revenue."
787	 *
788	 * Reads the same three metadata keys `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` dispatches on, so
789	 * "did this session fund a purchase" has one answer, not two.
790	 */
791	export function isPurchaseLegSession(metadata: Stripe.Metadata | null | undefined): boolean {
792	  return !!(
793	    metadata?.nxeonOrder ||
794	    metadata?.nxeonGameOrder ||
795	    metadata?.nxeonResize ||
796	    metadata?.nxeonDiskExpand ||
797	    metadata?.nxeonHostOrder ||
798	    metadata?.nxeonEmailOrder
799	  );
800	}
801	
802	/**
803	 * Credit a user's wallet for a completed Checkout session, idempotently.
804	 * Called from both the success-redirect confirm route (works without HTTPS)
805	 * and the webhook (belt-and-suspenders once HTTPS is available).
806	 * Returns true if a credit was applied this call.
807	 *
808	 * Takes the ALREADY-RETRIEVED session rather than an id: `fulfilCheckoutSession`
809	 * fetches it once and both the credit and the fulfilment routing read that single
810	 * object, so the two can never disagree about what this payment was (and a Stripe
811	 * read failure surfaces in one place, loudly, instead of four times as `null`).
812	 */
813	export async function creditCheckoutSession(session: Stripe.Checkout.Session): Promise<boolean> {
814	  const userId = session.metadata?.nxeonUserId;
815	  const cents = session.amount_total ?? 0;
816	  if (!userId || cents <= 0 || session.payment_status !== "paid") return false;
817	
818	  // Legacy guard: rows credited before `stripeSessionId` existed only recorded the
819	  // session id inside the description.
820	  const legacy = await db.walletTransaction.findFirst({
821	    where: { stripeSessionId: null, description: { contains: session.id } },
822	  });
823	  if (legacy) return false;
824	
825	  // Is this credit a product the customer bought, or the funding leg of something
826	  // else they bought? Only the first is a "Wallet top-up" and only the first gets
827	  // a billing document — see isPurchaseLegSession for the incident.
828	  const purchaseLeg = isPurchaseLegSession(session.metadata);
829	
830	  // Idempotency is enforced by the UNIQUE index on `stripeSessionId` — NOT by a
831	  // read-then-write check. The confirm-redirect and the webhook can arrive
832	  // concurrently (and /api/stripe/confirm is unauthenticated and replayable), so
833	  // only the database can safely decide the winner. P2002 == already credited.
834	  const ops: Prisma.PrismaPromise<unknown>[] = [
835	    db.walletTransaction.create({
836	      data: {
837	        userId,
838	        amountCents: cents,
839	        description: `Stripe payment (${session.id})`,
840	        stripeSessionId: session.id,
841	      },
842	    }),
843	    db.user.update({ where: { id: userId }, data: { balanceCents: { increment: cents } } }),
844	    db.notification.create({
845	      data: {
846	        userId,
847	        title: `Payment of $${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)} received`,
848	        href: "/dashboard/billing",
849	      },
850	    }),
851	  ];
852	  // Index of the invoice-create inside `ops`, or -1 when no invoice is issued
853	  // (a purchase leg). Used to recover the new invoice's id for the receipt email.
854	  let invoiceOpIndex = -1;
855	  if (!purchaseLeg) {
856	    // PAID invoice for the top-up. Created in the SAME guarded transaction as
857	    // the wallet credit, so the UNIQUE(stripeSessionId) constraint that makes
858	    // the credit idempotent also prevents a duplicate invoice on replay.
859	    //
860	    // A purchase leg is deliberately left undocumented HERE: the order, resize or
861	    // disk-expansion it funds issues the one invoice for the whole purchase, and
862	    // that document — not this one — is what the customer's card statement shows.
863	    // If the fulfilment then fails the money stays in the wallet as an ordinary
864	    // credit (ledger row + notification), and the invoice is issued by whatever it
865	    // is eventually spent on; inventing a top-up document at that point would
866	    // double-count the same dollars all over again the moment they deploy.
867	    // Remember WHERE in the batch this lands, so the created row's id can be read
868	    // back out of the transaction result. The receipt email promises the customer
869	    // an attached invoice, and it can only keep that promise if it knows the id.
870	    invoiceOpIndex = ops.length;
871	    ops.push(
872	      db.invoice.create({
873	        data: invoiceCreateData({
874	          userId,
875	          description: "Wallet top-up",
876	          status: "PAID",
877	          lineItems: [
878	            { description: "Wallet top-up", qty: 1, unitCents: cents, amountCents: cents },
879	          ],
880	        }),
881	      }),
882	    );
883	  }
884	  let invoiceId: string | undefined;
885	  try {
886	    const results = await db.$transaction(ops);
887	    if (invoiceOpIndex >= 0) {
888	      const created = results[invoiceOpIndex] as { id?: string } | undefined;
889	      invoiceId = created?.id;
890	    }
891	  } catch (e) {
892	    if ((e as { code?: string })?.code === "P2002") return false; // raced — already credited
893	    throw e;
894	  }
895	  // A funded wallet is the referred user's first paid action — reward both sides.
896	  try {
897	    const { maybeRewardReferral } = await import("./actions-growth");
898	    await maybeRewardReferral(userId);
899	  } catch { /* best-effort */ }
900	  try {
901	    const u = await db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } });
902	    if (u) {
903	      const { sendMail, emails } = await import("./mailer");
904	      // Say what the money was for. On a purchase leg it is emphatically NOT a
905	      // top-up, and a receipt that calls it one is the same false statement the
906	      // duplicate invoice used to make, just in the customer's inbox.
907	      // The third argument is the promise, and it is the truth: we claim an attached
908	      // invoice only when there is an invoice id to attach. A purchase leg issues no
909	      // top-up invoice (the order does), so its receipt points at billing history
910	      // instead of promising a file that was never generated.
911	      const tpl = emails.receipt(
912	        `$${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}`,
913	        purchaseLeg ? "your Nxeon order" : "wallet top-up",
914	        !!invoiceId,
915	      );
916	      // `kind` + `userId` hands this to the preference policy in lib/prefs.ts.
917	      // A receipt is ACCOUNT tier — suppressible by email if the customer turned
918	      // account email off. This is the one send site where that toggle actually
919	      // bites today, so it is the one that made the switch a lie.
920	      await sendMail({ to: u.email, subject: tpl.subject, html: tpl.html, userId, kind: "receipt", invoiceId });
921	    }
922	  } catch { /* best-effort */ }
923	  return true;
924	}
